 Order

Accused No.1 in Crime No.338/2023 registered by Jnanabharathi Police Station for the offence punishable under Sections 304B and 498A of IPC, is before this Court under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.
2.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

3. On the basis of the complaint dated 24.09.2023 lodged by Smt. Susheela, wife of Sri. Ramalinga,
FIR in Crime No.338/2023 was registered against the petitioner and three others by Jnanabharathi Police Station, Bengaluru City, for the aforesaid offences.
4. In the complaint, it is averred that complainant's daughter was married to petitioner on 06.04.2023.
At the time of marriage, complainant and her family members had given gold jewelry and other articles to the petitioner as demanded.
Initially, the petitioner and his family members were taking care of their daughter.
Subsequently, they started harassing and torturing complainant's daughter.
It is also alleged that the petitioner herein had illicit relationship with some other lady and therefore, there was a quarrel between him and his wife.

In NC: 2023:KHC:40928 the meanwhile,
complainant's daughter became pregnant and also gave birth to a child.

After delivering the child,
the complainant's daughter had gone back to her matrimonial home and on 23.09.2023,
complainant received a phone call and she was informed that her daughter had committed suicide and died.
In this background, she has lodged the complaint.
5. During the course of investigation of the case, the petitioner was arrested on 24.09.2023.

His bail application before the XLV Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru City in Crl. Misc.
No.9566/2023 was rejected on 20.10.2023.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Therefore, he is before this Court.

6. Learned Counsel for the petitioner reiterating the grounds urged in the petition submits that accused Nos.2 to 4 as against whom similar allegations are made, are granted anticipatory bail by a Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Crl.P.No.10618/2023.

He submits that major portion of the Venkateshan vs The State Of Karnataka By on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20069770/
2 investigation is complete and accordingly, prays to allow the petition.
7.

entities.text: Venkateshan vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent-State opposed the bail petition.

He submits that NC: 2023:KHC:40928 investigation is under progress and accordingly,
prays to dismiss the petition.

8. From a reading of the complaint averments, it is sent that there is no serious allegation against the accused persons with regard to the demand for dowry and the harassment meted out on the deceased in furtherance of such demand.
The allegations made in the complaint would go to show that the petitioner allegedly had illicit relationship with some other lady and therefore, there was a quarrel between the couple.
9. A Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Crl.P.No.10618/2023 has granted anticipatory bail to accused Nos.2 to 4.

In the said order, this Court has observed that from a perusal of the complaint averments, it is seen that there is no specific allegation against the petitioners that before marriage,
they have demanded any dowry, post-marriage, they have involved in subjecting the deceased to harassment for the purpose of dowry.
The petitioner has no criminal antecedents and he is in custody from 24.09.2023.
Major portion of the investigation is complete.

Under the circumstances,
I am of the NC: 2023:KHC:40928 opinion that the petitioner has made out a case for grant of regular bail.
Accordingly, the following order:-
10. The petition is allowed.
